blocks.text:
What follows is guesswork, of course, but it now looks possible that the killer headed for your town.

Whether the killer got in safely, or the landslide forced a return to this town, I can't yet say. If it's the latter, that's easy pickings for the bounty hunters.

Up north, the Kingdom of Asroit and the Duchy of Fakolz seem to be at odds again. Word is it began when the Duke of Fakolz insulted the face of Duke Ascania's daughter, Ascania being one of Asroit's four ducal houses.

The war of insults keeps heating up. Both dukes have now gathered their armies and are boasting that they'll march on the other.

However many troops they gather, it's plain this will end like the "July War" two hundred years ago, without a single sword crossed. Still, two countries squabbling over a thing like this... These times are so peaceful it leaves me speechless.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

The "Dragonet Orb" you sent me, I sold to a Bailestean noble at eight times the usual price.

It's been 40 years since the underground city of Asla Fael was found, and treasure that turns into a fortune as easily as it once did is getting scarce, as you'd expect. This time, for once, the deal had some real meat on it. I'll say my thanks here, for what it's worth.

That reminds me: the price of "Magic Tools" alone has held high and steady for over 20 years. Seventy percent of them seem to flow south.

In these peaceful times I do sometimes wonder what anyone wants with such things, but nobody complains when they sell this high. Keep sending them.

Next, a rundown of events around the world.

The chairman of the Republic of Baileste's Committee of Forty was murdered by terrorists of the Irenian independence movement.

Early this year the head of state's house caught fire, and six high government officials who had come to a party there died in the flames. That too was most likely the work of the Irenian independence movement.

The culprits in both cases have yet to be caught, but in reprisal the Republic of Baileste's government has reportedly carried off over 500 Irenians from the island of Irenia. No doubt they'll be shipped off to some mountain as labor again.

They say it's been over a thousand years since nations last fought nations, yet this sort of rot never goes away. No, lately I feel it's getting worse.

Maybe I've just gotten old, though...

Next, on to news from the north.

The trouble between Duke Ascania, one of Asroit's four dukes, and the Duchy of Fakolz was settled with money, as most expected. But the way it ended was rather amusing, so I'll set it down here.

For a while there was a rumor that Duke Durer, another of Asroit's four dukes, would join hands with the Duchy of Fakolz to catch Duke Ascania in a pincer. But it was the Duke of Fakolz, who supposedly had the upper hand, that backed down first.

This too is only rumor, but the only son of a certain Fakolz grandee took it into his head to invade Duke Ascania's lands all by himself, and instead got lost in the forest.

The Duke of Fakolz is said to have handed Duke Ascania a fortune to search for the man. To think they pay taxes for the sake of such dim-witted noble lords... I can't help but pity the people of Fakolz. No, every country's about the same, I suppose.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

Sorry this is so late. But I've been in no state to be sending letters.

One day some months ago, with no warning at all, monsters appeared all over the world. Confusion and terror have thrown the whole continent into panic. In one night this world turned into hell. It's been only a few months, yet it feels as if this hell has gone on for over ten years.

The Republic of Baileste's government sent troops everywhere, but they lose battle after battle and are apparently no use at all.

In the Kingdom of Asroit, not a single knight answers the king's summons. The king has had no choice but to conscript peasants, but with no weapons or food to issue them, they're beaten before they ever face a monster.

Perhaps peace simply went on too long. It seems to me everyone has forgotten how to fight.

Thanks to the monsters, the transport and messenger networks of us trading merchants are in tatters too. Of the Seven Highways only one is passable, and in big cities that grow little of their own food, like Baileste and Lenos, people are even starving to death. The Republic of Baileste's government seems to be gathering food by sea, but one thing is certain: it isn't going well. And even if food does arrive, it will never reach the common folk. It'll all end up in noble bellies, I suppose.

From our trading posts in other countries, not even a word. But the way things look, there may be no safe place left anywhere.

This town of Lanz has only days left, too. Eyeless two-legged lizards, giant red bats, long-headed monsters with cries like monkeys... There must have been a hundred all told... We couldn't have failed to notice them, yet before we knew it they were all over town, damn them. At this point gates and walls mean nothing.

We've now taken refuge in a monastery in the forest, but I doubt even half the townsfolk got out. The rest all became food for those things. Of all those many officials, not one is left -- though more of them ran than got eaten.

This was my first time back in Lanz since it became a monster den, and by good fortune the building that holds the Transporter hasn't been wrecked by them.

It took me nearly a month to find a safe route, but from now on I should be able to pass on new information as it comes in. Provided I'm still alive, of course.

I wish us both good luck.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

Astounding news.

The monsters before us did not just appear out of nowhere. They are us: humans, changed.

There have long been rumors of it, but honestly I didn't much believe them. Once you see a person turn into a monster with your own eyes, though, you have no choice.

We still don't know what turns people into monsters, and meanwhile a rumor is spreading that I'm sorry to say is bad news for you: that anyone who has set foot in Kars Bastide even once is sure to turn into a monster.

In the Kingdom of Asroit, the Kingdom of Racoss and parts of the Duchy of Fakolz, anyone with the slightest tie to the Coffin of Kars is reportedly being executed, one after another, without trial. I'm sure the rumor is groundless, but the Church is fanning it, so there's no stopping it.

Here in Lanz, so closely tied to your town, nothing like that goes on, naturally. But even if you do manage to get out of town, you'd best stay away from home for a while.

Next, the state of each country, as far as I can tell.

The Republic of Baileste's government has decided to withdraw its troops from its territories. It is massing all its forces, navy and army alike, in the capital, Baileste.

They're reportedly hauling every last bit of food and every weapon off to the capital. In other words, the territories have been abandoned. In fact, in Bania and West Sefita they'd form militias to protect themselves from monsters, but they haven't got the weapons to start with.

Baileste's rule has finally ended, and with it came what they longed for, the independence and reunification of their homelands. Now monsters and hunger fall on them without mercy.

In Asroit, the regional lords and clans have ignored the king's call. Each gathers troops and has begun fighting the monsters separately. "What do I care about somebody else's land?" is surely what they really think.

It's as if over 100 countries, great and small, have sprung up inside one. And those armies don't only flex their muscle at monsters: skirmishes between the lords are on the rise, too.

Standing out among these lords are, as you'd expect, the four dukes: Pfalz, Durer, Ascania and Wettin. All four are already stronger than the king. The royal capital, Gasnitz, on the other hand, has been left stripped bare, the lords having pulled their troops back to their own lands.

In the Kingdom of Racoss, monsters reportedly appeared at a banquet hosted by the king. The king, of course, and most of the nobles at court were eaten. The lucky survivors, and the lesser nobles who weren't invited, are seizing ownerless castles left and right in the chaos. Looting a house on fire, if ever I saw it.

On the island of Irenia, the Republic of Baileste has abandoned the island's north, so they're reportedly giddy at finally having their longed-for independence.

The trouble is, as I wrote above, that the Republic's garrison took all the food and weapons with it. How many thousands will starve before the next harvest... And just as pitiable are the residents of Bailestean stock left behind. Two peoples' ordeal is only now beginning.

The Fisano City-State League seems to be using this opening to filch cities in southern Racoss and western Baileste. Fisano folk haven't got the "u" of "unity" in them, but at times like this they move awfully fast.

It's said the Duchy of Fakolz may invade Asroit. Given the two countries' history, that's no great surprise.

The Kingdoms of Luminia, Krasdar and Biastok, and then Tradoa... I have no news yet from these far-flung countries. I know nothing of the interior of the Kingdom of Sefita either, or of Asroit north of Gasnitz.

I'll write if anything comes up. Don't hold your breath.
Olterna E. Tassel, Tassel Trading House

To the residents of the Coffin of Kars

News from the various countries has been pouring in since my last letter.

The Kingdom of Asroit has in effect ceased to exist. And what brought down this kingdom of 1,500 years was not monsters but humans. The detached palace at Lanitz, where the king had fled, was attacked by fewer than twenty mountain bandits after treasure, and the royal family was wiped out... Not one soldier stayed to guard the king at his end, it seems. A wretched finish. Serves them right, though.

In sharp contrast to the fall of the royal house, the four dukes are gaining ever more momentum. And war among those four dukes is at last beginning in earnest. Strength aside, the most famous is surely House Durer in the east... The "Red Lion Knights" formed by Duke Durer's sons: their ill fame reaches even this distant town, more than I'd like.

Where the Red Lion Knights have passed, things are reportedly worse than anything monsters leave. Village after village with no part in it is burned, and young women and all the food are carried off. In Kassel, a regional city in South Asroit, 30,000 citizens were reportedly massacred. Yet when they do find an actual monster, they flee headlong -- how very like nobles.

In Baileste, troops recalled from the territories have done well, and the monsters in the city center have mostly been wiped out. But what came next was worse: this time the soldiers from the territories and the mercenaries have risen in revolt.

When southern bumpkins see the wealth of Baileste and the slackness of the First Fleet, supposedly the mainstay of its military, you can't blame them for revolting. Even so, it's no laughing matter. More units keep joining the revolt, and the whole city has become a battlefield.

The vast lands Baileste once ruled have now, like Asroit, split into many pieces. Unlike Asroit, though, nearly all of Baileste's nobles were in the capital, so the provinces fall to the citizens' councils of their regional cities. Majority-rule councils, the Bailesteans' great love. But everyone just flaps about, decisions come late and no one will take responsibility. In peacetime perhaps, but for these turbulent times they're simply unfit. Maybe that's why shady types are popping up too, such as ex-bandits who call themselves emperor.

The changing of humans into monsters should have fallen off quite a bit lately compared with its peak, but another problem has suddenly come up: the revival of the "Holy Tribunal".

The fear that the person next door might turn into a monster at any moment must be what brought this thing back. No proper trial, just guilty and immediate death... Let someone inform the Church that "that one's going to turn into a monster," and that person's death is sealed.
